searchText: Turns out the best descendant is very useful when it comes to filtering the block tree I re-read the spec and the bounce attack last night and realised I missed a detail in my impl. I think I just managed to fix it; allowing to traverse through lower justified epochs in order to reach the target ones Thanks Paul. Your code comments are great. Makes it really easy to understand I'm transcribing some of your work and proto's work into a Prysm design doc for my team to understand better. Feel free to take a look or edit if necessary: https://hackmd.io/@tchain/S1MoETog8/edit I recommend not using Go pointers within proto-node It's already all in an array, and pruning is much easier if you can adjust indices after shifting/modifying/slicing the array Also, raw indices make persisting the array really easy, so you can store/load it from disk for quick starts <@!363800010518822915> nice summary, will read it more and see if anything else can be improved Updated with a small fix, typos and note on pointers vs indices Thank you! I'll put a few more hours on it. Still going through Paul's PR. Really excited to integrate this to run time And note on array order, the core reason why it all works in one iteration over the array And Rust is kind of cheating with the Option integer type that fits just in uint64 (not sure if Paul changed it, but it could be done like that). Zero cost abstraction, almost as nice as a pointer, but serializing well. In Go we just have to assign some special value and deal with it 😦 I guess that's why you have `nonExistentNode` for `^uint64(0)`... not gonna lie, I'm slowly becoming a fan of rust It’s never too late to join the Rust family! 😉 Call in 15 min? Great call today <@!203220829473996800> <@!361447803194441738> . Here's my wip branch for proto array fork choice: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/4559 Still far from completion but good start. Feel free to take a look and point out anything you dont like : ) <@!363800010518822915> nice. And although it's cool to see my old "proto array" algorithm doing so well, credits to Paul for refactoring it to production-quality, and supporting the tree-filter-branch stuff. Now just don't forget to port over the tail end of changes in his PR, there are some important bugfixes in there.

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: It's already all in an array, and pruning is much easier if you can adjust indices after shifting/modifying/slicing the array

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Also, raw indices make persisting the array really easy, so you can store/load it  from disk for quick starts
